metadata.title: PeerScore — the open researcher index
metadata.description: Open-source index of researchers worldwide with LLM-powered publication analysis.

header.searchPlaceholder: Search a researcher, a field, an institution

footer.notice: Analyses are generated by language models and can contain errors · Content available under an open license

home.title: The open encyclopedia of research output.
home.intro: PeerScore indexes researchers worldwide and asks several language models to read their publications with a prompt written for their field. Every score, rationale and disagreement is public.
home.papersModels: {papers, plural, one {# paper} other {# papers}} · {models, plural, one {# model} other {# models}}
home.noAnalysis: No analysis has been published yet. The first submission in the queue will appear here.

1.title: Submit a name
1.body: Anyone can submit a researcher. One field, no account — the request joins a public queue.

2.title: Publications are collected
2.body: A worker resolves the researcher in open scholarly records and downloads publication metadata and abstracts.

3.title: Field-specific analysis
3.body: Several language models read the publications with a prompt written for the field and score five criteria independently.

4.title: The article goes live
4.body: Scores are aggregated into a weighted consensus and the full write-up, with every disagreement, is published within 24–48 h.

home.reproducibleBody: Prompts are versioned and hashed, model outputs are stored verbatim, and the whole pipeline is open source. Analyses are generated by language models and can contain errors — report one from any article page.

researchers.title: Index of researchers
researchers.intro: Every researcher in PeerScore, published or waiting in the queue. Scores are weighted consensus values from several language models.

submit.title: Submit a researcher
submit.intro: One field, no account. The request joins a public queue and the article is published automatically once the analysis completes.

1.title: Queued
1.body: Your request is stored with a public id and a position in the queue. Nothing else is collected about you.

2.title: Publications collected
2.body: A worker resolves the name in open scholarly records and downloads publication metadata, abstracts and code links.

3.title: Field-specific analysis
3.body: Several language models read the publications with a prompt written for the field and score five criteria independently.

4.title: Article published
4.body: The scores are aggregated, the write-up and every disagreement are published, and the page goes live automatically.

eligible.1: Any researcher with publicly indexed publications (journals, conferences, preprints).
eligible.2: Living or deceased, active or retired — the analysis reads the published record only.
eligible.3: Names are resolved in open scholarly records; if several people share a name, the best-documented match is used and shown in the infobox.
eligible.4: No private data is used: nothing beyond publication metadata, abstracts and public code repositories.
eligible.5: Duplicate requests are merged; a researcher already in the index is linked instead of queued again.

submit.nameHelp: Full name as it appears on publications. We resolve it in open scholarly records; add an initial or an institution if the name is common.
submit.errorTooShort: The name must be at least {min} characters long.
submit.errorTooLong: The name must be at most {max} characters long.
submit.errorInvalid: The name must contain letters or digits.
submit.errorServer: Something went wrong while queuing the request. Please try again.
submit.queuedBody: Publications will be collected from open scholarly sources and analyzed by several language models with the prompt written for the field. The article is usually published within 24–48 hours.
submit.existsBody: A researcher with this name already has a page. Open it to read the analysis, or request a re-analysis from the article page if it looks out of date.

queue.title: Public queue
queue.intro: Every request that has not been published yet, oldest first. <n>{count}</n> waiting. This page refreshes itself every minute; articles go live within 24–48 h.

notFound.title: This page is not in the index.
notFound.body: The researcher may not have been submitted yet, or the address is wrong. You can search the index or queue a new analysis.
